newsitem.title: USA: Arlington, Texas, sells $40.9 mln of bonds.
newsitem.headline: Arlington, Texas, sells $40.9 mln of bonds.

text.p: The city of Arlington on Tuesday sold two series of 20-year capital improvement bonds totaling about $40.9 million, officials said.
Chuck Springer, debt administrator for the city located between Dallas and Fort Worth, said the first issue of $33.9 million were general obligation bonds previously approved by voters.
They were priced at 4.92 percent by Goldman Sachs & Co. along with Lehman Brothers and J.P. Morgan Securities Inc.

The second issue for $6.9 million were a combination of tax and revenue certificates of obligation authorized by the city council, not requiring voter approval. They were priced at 5.048 percent by Prudential Securities Inc.
"We are real pleased at the low interest rates for both," Springer told Reuters. "We had 11 bids for the general obligation bonds and five for the certificates of obligation."

Of the $33.9 million general obligation bonds, $22.8 million will be used for roads and sidewalks and the rest will go for a library, parks and recreation improvements, traffic signal upgrades and the fire department, Finance Director Jack Eastwood said.
He said $4.8 million of the certificates of obligation will be spent on building a recreation center on the city's north side and for a fourth golf course.

Another $1.15 million will go for a computer dispatch center for the police and fire departments. The rest will go for additional hangars at Arlington Municipal Airport and for architectural plans for expansion of the city's convention center.
Last month, the city sold $38.1 million in water and sewer bonds which were also priced below five percent.
